q: For "next greater element", the stack's values from bottom to top are…
why: Anything smaller than the new value gets popped (answered), so what remains is decreasing.

q: Why is the monotonic stack O(n) despite the while loop?
options: The while loop runs at most once
Each index is pushed once and popped at most once overall
The stack is bounded by k
why: Count pushes and pops over the whole run: at most 2n.

q: Daily Temperatures asks "how many days until warmer". What should the stack store?
why: The answer is a distance, so you need the index: i − j.
3 is the next greater for both 2 and 1; nothing is greater than 3.

q: "Maximum of every window of size k" in O(n). Which structure?
options: A monotonic decreasing deque of indexes
why: Back: drop smaller values (useless). Front: drop indexes outside the window. Front = max.

q: Largest Rectangle in Histogram: when a bar is popped from an increasing stack, what have you just found?
options: Its right boundary (the first shorter bar) and, from the new top, its left boundary
why: Both nearest-shorter neighbours are known at pop time, so the widest rectangle with that height is known.
